html:
Hurricane Katrina was a huge storm that struck the Gulf Coast of the United States in late August 2005. It flooded most of New Orleans and killed about 1,400 people.

It hit land on 29 August in Louisiana and Mississippi. New Orleans lies mostly below sea level, protected by levees and floodwalls. The storm surge broke through them in dozens of places, and about 80 percent of the city went under water, in places several metres deep. Investigations later blamed poor design by the Army Corps of Engineers.

Many of the poorest residents, most of them Black, had no car and could not leave. Thousands sheltered for days in the Superdome and the convention centre with little food or water. The slow response of the Federal Emergency Management Agency and of President George W. Bush became a national scandal.

With damage of about $125 billion, Katrina was the costliest storm in US history. Hundreds of thousands of people left the region, and New Orleans had far fewer people for years after.
sum: Hurricane Katrina was a huge storm that struck the Gulf Coast of the United States in late August 2005. It flooded most of New Orleans and killed about 1,400 people.
